audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Gragas six of seven stages while the entry's own whys describe Cho'Gath taking over from level 3 and the win rate is 57.5% over 160 games.
audit.why: Gragas only has level 2, where Body Slam (14s at rank 1) lets him dive, land an empowered Drunken Rage auto and dash out before Rupture resolves. From 3 Feral Scream locks that escape, and from 6 Feast is true damage his Drunken Rage reduction does nothing about.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Gragas / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath, and difficulty dropped to 5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phase whys were the generic template and named no cooldown; the level-6 line said only 'Gragas's ultimate changes the math too'.
audit.why: Feast is 80/70/60s true damage plus permanent max HP. Explosive Cask is 100/85/70s — a 100-second rank-1 cooldown is the largest window in the lane and the thing to fight around. Body Slam at 14s rank 1 is the trading metronome.
audit.corrected: Phase whys now carry Barrel Roll 10s, Body Slam 14s, Explosive Cask 100s and Feast 80s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Interaction fields said only 'His engage. Q-peel after it.' The decisive interaction — that a silenced Gragas cannot cast Body Slam to leave — was never stated, and one field described Cho'Gath as leaving him 'grounded', which is not in his kit.
audit.why: Feral Scream (W, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, 300 cone) silences. Body Slam (E, 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s) is his only escape, so a silence lands him a full 14 seconds with no exit. Rupture (Q, flat 6s, 950) pops him airborne, which takes him out of a Body Slam charge. Important limit: the silence stops him hand-detonating Barrel Roll, but Riot's text says the cask explodes on its own after 4 seconds regardless.
audit.corrected: Silence him and Body Slam is locked for 14s — but Barrel Roll still self-detonates at 4s.

audit.why: Anti-heal is genuinely called for here: Happy Hour heals him on every skill cast, and the missing-interactions file flags Grievous Wounds timing as deciding extended trades. The entry already carries the anti-heal line.

edits.before: Farm with E spikes and respect everything — you scale, he rents. Identify how Gragas contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Barrel Roll (10s at rank 1, 850 range) pokes and Happy Hour heals it back — match CS at range and commit nothing he can sidestep.

edits.before: W silence starts flipping his combo windows. Only take the trade when Gragas's Body Slam is down.
edits.after: His one real window: Body Slam in, empowered Drunken Rage auto, then dash out before Rupture lands.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gragas must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Rupture into Feral Scream is online — knock him up, silence the Body Slam escape, and he is stuck for its 14 seconds.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Body Slam's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Carnivore kill-heals and Vorpal Spikes out-attrition Happy Hour — the longer the trade runs the further ahead you are.

edits.before: Feast stacks turn you into terrain — every R is permanent HP plus a true-damage execute. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gragas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast (80s) is true damage: Drunken Rage's reduction and his HP bar barely touch it, while Explosive Cask sits on 100s at rank 1. Commit on that gap.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Body Slam's cooldown.
edits.after: Heartsteel plus a Feast stack: his AP brawl bounces off, and Feast still executes him.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Gragas carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: He has no true or percent-HP damage, so stacked Feast makes you unkillable to him while Feast still executes him outright.

edits.before: Track Gragas's Body Slam: His engage. Q-peel after it. When it is down — Q-W + R him.
edits.after: Silence him and Body Slam is locked for 14s — but Barrel Roll still self-detonates at 4s.

edits.before: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — His engage. Q-peel after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gragas Body Slam: matchup-defining — 14s at rank 1, and Feral Scream locks it out entirely. Rupture pops him out of the charge. Explosive Cask is 100s at rank 1. - Feast: kill windows only.

edits.before: Q under Gragas's feet as he commits, W-silence the answer, and E-spike the trade — your sustain regens what his chip cost.
edits.after: Rupture him out of the Body Slam charge, Feral Scream so he cannot dash back out, then E-spike — 14s with no escape is a kill.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Body Slam and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. The lane is decided by whether Feral Scream lands before he Body Slams back out.

edits.before: Land Rupture to knock him up, then chain Feral Scream so the silence stops him Q-pool-healing or comboing while he's grounded and waiting on Body Slam
edits.after: Land Rupture to knock him up, then chain Feral Scream so the silence stops him Q-pool-healing and locks Body Slam out for its full 14 seconds

notes: Packet flagged wants.foe[2] 'Save Explosive Cask' as a probable wrong name — false positive, that is the real ability name. wants.you[0] previously said the silence left him 'grounded'; Cho'Gath has no ground in his kit, so I replaced it with the actual effect (Body Slam locked out). Cho'Gath's kit file flags Rupture as 'grounding'; Riot's description says it pops enemies into the air, so I wrote it as a knockup. Left level 2 with Gragas rather than the packet's 'Skill' — the existing why argues the Body Slam in-and-out convincingly and I would rather not flatten a correct read.
